assessments.reasoning: Five contiguous ranges cover the 73,836-byte SPDX json/details record at the tagged commit, with reported SHA-256 e8d048eeb2eb042ec0437ca2b7b360baef48eaec7fb9e4e9b792aaf9ed33794b. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 3 gives licenseId=GPL-2.0-only, its comment and header. Its cited GNU HTML and text, OSI and OpenJDK URLs are references. The generated text uses a Boston address where the acquired GNU publisher text uses a URL.

The GitHub API for spdx/license-list-data identifies 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as the annotated v3.29.0 tag object. Its target is a commit with SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the revision in the generated record URL. The API reports the tag as unsigned.

The digest-matched GNU text supplies edition and notice context. Section 0 identifies the copyright holder's notice. Section 9 makes the later-version option conditional, and the appendix illustrates that option. The publisher copy supplies no specimen of a particular project's version-2-only grant.

challenge.method: Tested whether the common license body, the FSF appendix, or a positive SPDX cross-reference match could distinguish the two identifiers. Compared both complete generated records, including their comments, matching templates and standard headers.
challenge.results: Both records reproduce the later-option appendix, share the first 16,384 bytes, and report a match to the same OpenJDK LICENSE at commit 6162e2c5213c5dd7c1127fd9616b543efa898962. Those witnesses cannot distinguish the elections. The version-2-only header and the SPDX comment resolve the apparent conflict. A license-text match alone cannot establish the grant for every OpenJDK file.

limitations: “Granting use” is shorthand for the version election. The specimen notice actually speaks of redistributing and/or modifying the program. “SPDX License List 3.29.0 lists GPL-2.0-only for code whose applicable notice specifies GNU GPL version 2 alone” states the correspondence more precisely.

Both proposed crosswalks have the same subject, edition and structured scope, and both conditions arrays are empty. Their statements preserve their respective notice conditions. Reading the structured values alone as unconditional aliases would lose that distinction. The authority field identifies the license publisher, while SPDX controls list membership.
A particular project's applicable notice must establish its grant, version election, modifications and file coverage.
reasoning: SPDX License List 3.29.0 lists GPL-2.0-only for code whose applicable notice specifies GPL version 2 alone. The exact identifier, explanatory comment, and standard header agree. The apparent inconsistency is that licenseText in this same entry includes an “or later” notice. SPDX expressly identifies that passage as the example in the application appendix. The entry's separate standardLicenseHeader specifies “version 2.”
